Collections

Three collection families

A good aquatic display is a composition: something that moves, a landscape that grows and a structure that holds it together. Start with the family you need, or read how they work together below.

  • 01Ornamental Fish
  • 02Aquatic Plants
  • 03Driftwood

01 Collection

Ornamental Fish

Fish bring movement and colour to a composition. This family is presented as studies of form and finnage, with selection framed as questions to discuss rather than a stock list.

  • Colour and finnage
  • Form and movement
  • Community fit
Explore ornamental fish

02 Collection

Aquatic Plants

Plants build depth and atmosphere. This family is organised around how foliage shapes a scape — layer, leaf form, colour and texture — not around a catalogue of species.

  • Layer and depth
  • Leaf form and texture
  • Colour contrast
Explore aquatic plants

03 Collection

Driftwood

Driftwood is the structure of a scape. Each piece is discussed by its lines, branching and mass, and by how its surface reads under water and light.

  • Line and branching
  • Mass and scale
  • Surface and tone
Explore driftwood

How the families differ

Each family does a different job.

01Ornamental Fish

Role in a display
The moving focal point that draws the eye first.
What to look at
Colour depth, fin condition, how the fish carries itself.
A question to bring
Which other inhabitants and what display size are planned?
Ornamental Fish

02Aquatic Plants

Role in a display
The landscape: depth, softness and a sense of scale.
What to look at
Leaf shape, density, colour and how growth fills space.
A question to bring
Which layer needs work, and what mood should the scape carry?
Aquatic Plants

03Driftwood

Role in a display
The skeleton: lines, scale and the main direction of movement.
What to look at
Silhouette, branching, surface texture and tone.
A question to bring
What are the display dimensions and the intended viewing side?
Driftwood
